title: Re-verify the two held legs: a corpus that says +6.11R and +2.80R against recorded live results of -86R and -13.933R
note:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-22: 'wire 2 and investigate the other 2'. TWO LEGS HELD OFF bybit_2 pending this row. [!] fade_breakout_4h -- DEMOTED 2026-06-01 (Tier-3, operator): 'no live edge demonstrated -- 16 closed trades, 44% win, net -86R (almost all bybit_1 demo; real-money bybit_2 +1.55/8)', and its condition reads 'Re-promote only on a fresh net-positive LIVE/SHADOW WINDOW'. The R7 corpus grades it +6.1101R over n=25, 3 of 4 folds. A BACKTEST IS A DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT FROM A LIVE/SHADOW WINDOW and does not satisfy that condition literally. [!] htf_pullback_trend_2h -- DEMOTED 2026-08-23 (Tier-3, operator): '4-axis tune discharge found nothing... Baseline itself is OOS net_R -13.933, the worst of the pullback family, and this leg routes to bybit_2 (REAL MONEY)'. The R7 corpus grades it +2.7979R over n=80, 3 of 4 folds. [!] THE QUESTION IS ONE QUESTION COVERING BOTH, and it is not 'which leg is better': WHY DOES THE NEW CORPUS DISAGREE SO VIOLENTLY WITH THE PRIOR MEASUREMENTS, AND WHICH INSTRUMENT IS RIGHT? The benign answer is that the old numbers were LIVE/PAPER P&L and the new ones are BACKTESTS net of cost -- under the ladder a live book never establishes edge, so the backtest is the admissible instrument and both legs promote. THAT ANSWER MUST BE ESTABLISHED, NOT ASSUMED: check whether the -13.933R figure was itself a backtest (the 2026-08-23 note calls it 'baseline OOS net_R', which SOUNDS like a harness number, not live P&L -- if so the benign reading collapses and two harness runs on the same leg disagree by 16.7R). [!] WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THESE TWO: if a harness can produce -13.933R and +2.7979R for the same leg, that bears on how much weight the OTHER 32 passing records carry, including the two just wired. This row is cheap and its blast radius is the whole corpus. [!] 2026-09-22, PARTLY ANSWERED WITHOUT A NEW RUN — from the fold_detail that was already committed. htf_pullback_trend_2h: +4.09 -> +0.58 -> +0.88 -> -2.75, so the +2.7979R pooled is fold 1 and the last nine months are -1.29R. THE CONTRADICTION WITH THE 2026-08-23 DEMOTION ('OOS net_R -13.933') IS LARGELY EXPLAINED RATHER THAN OPEN: the leg is DECAYING, and the August demotion was made INSIDE the fold that is negative. Two numbers over different windows on a decaying leg do not have to agree, and the newer one being higher is not evidence it is better. fade_breakout_4h: +3.75 -> +3.17 -> +4.24 -> -5.05 — consistent for three folds and then collapsing, and its demotion condition ('re-promote only on a fresh net-positive LIVE/SHADOW WINDOW') is still not satisfied by a backtest. [!] SO THIS ROW'S REMAINING QUESTION IS NARROWER: not 'which number is right' but 'does either leg have an edge in the RECENT window'. That is exactly RQ-20260922-012's population question, and this row should be read after it rather than re-deriving it per leg. Neither leg moves off shadow in the meantime. [!] A THIRD LEG JOINS THEM: avax_pullback_2h, withdrawn from R8 before merge for the same reason, now carried by RQ-20260922-013.
